questions.q: Impermanent loss is the gap between an LP position's value and what?
options: The value of the pool's LP token at its all-time high
The protocol's total trading fee revenue for the day
What the LP would have if they had simply held the two assets separately instead of depositing them
The value of a completely unrelated, uncorrelated asset
questions.explain: IL is specifically defined relative to the "HODL alternative" — simply holding the deposited assets rather than providing liquidity with them.

questions.q: In the worked example, after ETH's price doubles from 2,000 to 4,000 USDC, what is the impermanent loss on the 100 ETH / 200,000 USDC pool?
options: 0 USDC — IL only happens when price falls, not rises
Exactly -200,000 USDC (-50%)
About -34,314.60 USDC (roughly -5.72%)
questions.explain: Pool value after rebalancing is 565,685.40 versus a HODL value of 600,000 — a gap of about -34,314.60, or -5.72%.

questions.q: Why does a price falling to half its original value produce the same IL percentage as a price doubling?
options: Because IL is calculated based on how far the price ratio moved away from 1, not which direction it moved
Because AMM pools automatically correct for price direction
This is incorrect — a price halving always produces a larger loss than doubling
Because fees always exactly offset any downward price movement
questions.explain: The IL formula depends on the ratio between new and old price; a ratio of 2 (doubling) and a ratio of 0.5 (halving) produce the same magnitude of loss.

questions.q: What makes impermanent loss become permanent?
options: Simply waiting long enough without ever withdrawing
Withdrawing from the pool while the price ratio is still different from the deposit ratio
The protocol team manually converting the loss into a permanent one
Earning trading fees while the price ratio is different from deposit
questions.explain: If the price ratio reverts back to the deposit ratio before you withdraw, the loss disappears. Withdrawing while it's still different locks the loss in.

questions.q: What is the one thing that's supposed to make providing liquidity worthwhile despite impermanent loss?
options: A legal guarantee against any loss
The fact that IL is always smaller than any possible fee income
Trading fee income (and, as later lessons cover, extra token incentives)
A government-backed insurance fund covering all LP losses
questions.explain: The lesson notes LPs need fee income — and later, extra token incentives — to make the IL cost of providing liquidity worthwhile at all.
